evals.name: signup-screen-reader-fix
evals.prompt: Support ticket from a blind user: they couldn't finish signing up with their screen reader. Fix the signup page so it works with a screen reader and a keyboard, and make sure CI catches it if it regresses.
evals.expected_output: The server-rendered signup flow (src/views/signup.js, public/signup.js, public/styles.css, the shared src/views/layout.js, and the welcome page it lands on) is fixed: real labels with autocomplete purposes, every validated control exposed as required, native radios in a named group that work without JavaScript as ADR 0002 requires, errors tied to each control including the radios, an error state a screen reader user hears on arrival without relying on script, copy from docs/design/signup-copy.md on the icon and dialog buttons, the submit button's hiding aria-label gone, a real dialog with focus handling and a terms link that works without scripts, no positive tabindex, a visible focus indicator with 3:1 contrast, a 24 px toggle target, text contrast for --muted (2.54:1) and --error (2.77:1) and non-text contrast for the 1.24:1 --border that docs/design/tokens.md calls decorative, with the tokens document corrected, and html lang. A node:test regression check under make check with no new npm dependency fails when a label or describedby is removed. make check passes; the reports page is left alone; the unescaped name in the welcome page is reported; nothing is committed or written outside the repository and the run's scratch folder; the final message says which checks were not run in a browser or with a screen reader, including the dialog's focus handling.
expectations: `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository, and it still runs the five tests from the fixture's test/validate.test.js and test/signup-page.test.js (an assertion may be updated for new markup, none deleted)

In the signup page rendered by src/views/signup.js, the name, email and password inputs each have a programmatically associated visible label (a label element tied by for and id, or wrapping the input) using the wording in docs/design/signup-copy.md (Full name, Work email, Password), a placeholder alone does not count; and they carry autocomplete values that identify their purpose (name, email, and new-password for the password), as WCAG 2.2 1.3.5 Identify input purpose requires

The plan picker is no longer div elements with tabindex="0" plus a hidden input set by public/signup.js: it is native radio inputs named plan inside a fieldset with a legend (or an element with role radiogroup and an accessible name), so a plan can be chosen and submitted with the keyboard and with JavaScript disabled, as docs/adr/0002-server-rendered-no-dependencies.md requires; a fix that only adds role and a Space key handler to the divs does not satisfy this

Every control the server rejects when empty (see src/validate.js: name, email, password, plan and terms) is exposed as required to assistive technology before the user submits: the required attribute or aria-required on each text input and the terms checkbox, and on the plan radios (or aria-required on an element with role radiogroup); the form's novalidate may stay. A plan group with no required state fails this, even when the other four controls have it

The terms checkbox is labelled by its text (the span with a click handler becomes a label for the checkbox, or aria-labelledby points to it), and the submit button's accessible name contains its visible text Create account (the aria-label="Submit form" is removed or replaced by one that starts with the visible text)

The icon-only password visibility button has the accessible name Show password from docs/design/signup-copy.md, and when the password is visible that name changes to Hide password (or aria-pressed reflects the state); a name invented from the code, such as toggle or eye, does not count
The password visibility button's target is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels (it is 20 by 20 in public/styles.css), or the run reports it as failing 2.5.8 Target size and says why it was left

In the error state rendered by signupPage with errors for every field, each invalid text input and the terms checkbox carry aria-invalid="true" and an aria-describedby containing the id of its own error message; each plan radio (not only the fieldset) references the plan error the same way; the password input's aria-describedby also references the hint; and aria-invalid is not placed on the fieldset alone, since its group role does not support it (on the radios, or on an element with role radiogroup, is fine)

In the error state a screen reader user is told the submission failed when the page loads, before reaching the fields, and this does not depend on client script (ADR 0002): the server-rendered document title changes (for example starts with Error), or a server-rendered error summary at the top of the form or main content names or links to the fields in error and receives focus without script (for example autofocus on a tabindex="-1" container), or both. A summary that is only focused by public/signup.js counts only if the title also changes; errors shown only next to each field do not satisfy this. Each summary link, if present, points to an id that exists on the page (the plan link to a radio or the fieldset)

The terms dialog is exposed as a dialog (a dialog element, or role="dialog" with aria-modal and an accessible name from its heading), focus moves into it when it opens, Escape closes it, focus returns to the Read the terms link on close, and its close button (currently a bare ×) has the name Close terms from the copy doc

The Read the terms link works with JavaScript disabled, as ADR 0002 requires: its href points to a real page or an in-page target holding the terms text, not href="#"; or the run reports the dead link as an open finding
The tabindex="1" on the email input is removed and no element on the signup page has a positive tabindex, and the html element in src/views/layout.js gets lang="en"

The global `*:focus { outline: none; }` in public/styles.css is removed or replaced so every focusable control on the signup page, the plan radios included, shows a visible focus indicator, and that indicator's colour contrasts at least 3:1 with the white background it sits on (1.4.11 Non-text contrast); an indicator in --border or --muted, or a browser default left unstyled next to a custom radio that hides the native one, does not count

The run finds that --muted #9ca3af on the white background measures about 2.5:1 and --error #f87171 about 2.8:1, both below the 4.5:1 needed for the 14 px hint and error text, changes them in public/styles.css to colours that reach at least 4.5:1 on #ffffff, and states the measured ratios

The run finds that the input borders (--border #e5e7eb, about 1.2:1 on white) are the only visual boundary of the text fields and fail 1.4.11 Non-text contrast (3:1), although docs/design/tokens.md labels that token decorative; it either darkens the field borders to at least 3:1 or reports this as an open finding with the measured ratio

docs/design/tokens.md, which claims 4.6:1 for --muted and 4.5:1 for --error and calls --border decorative, is corrected to the real ratios of the colours now in use, or the final message names each contradiction explicitly

A regression check runs under make check (so in the CI job in .gitlab-ci.yml). The grader verifies it by mutation, restoring the file after each: removing the for attribute from the email label (or the label element) in src/views/signup.js makes make check fail; removing the aria-describedby from the email input in the error state makes it fail; removing the legend from the plan group (or its accessible name, if a radiogroup is used) makes it fail; making signupPage return a page with no form controls makes it fail. A check that passes any of these mutations fails this expectation

package.json gains no dependency or devDependency (ADR 0002 forbids them without a security review); if the run recommends browser-level checks such as axe with Playwright, it says they need that review and does not add them
src/views/reports.js is not changed (it is outside the signup flow); mentioning its missing alt text is fine
The run reports, or fixes by escaping, that src/views/welcome.js interpolates the submitted name into the page without escaping (a reflected XSS on the page the signup flow lands on)

The final message states which checks were not performed, for example that no screen reader was used and whether the page was exercised in a real browser with the keyboard; if the terms dialog's focus handling (focus moves in, Escape closes it, focus returns to the link) was not exercised in a browser, it says so rather than presenting that behaviour as verified; and it does not claim the signup page is WCAG conformant or verified with a screen reader on the strength of code changes alone

The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree (a printed commit or push command for the user to run is fine)

The run writes nothing outside the output repository except in the scratch folder the harness gave the run (used as HOME, for temporary files or for backups), judged from the transcript and the parent directory. Files a browser tool writes into its own working directory without the run choosing that location are not held against the run; files the run itself creates or edits anywhere else, such as under the real home directory or in another repository, fail this
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: mobile-audit-for-client
evals.prompt: The payroll client's procurement wants an accessibility audit of the mobile app before they sign. Go through the app, write up what fails, and fix whatever's quick.
evals.expected_output: A written audit of the Expo React Native app covering all five screens (Home, Activity, Settings, Send and the dynamic app/receipt/[id].tsx) plus the icon-only tab bar in app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx, each finding with its file and the WCAG criterion, with measured contrast for theme.muted (2.64:1), theme.error (3.76:1) and the 1.24:1 border used for input outlines and the off Toggle track, and no false failure for success (5.02:1) or accent (6.7:1). Quick fixes land at the source: IconButton gets a role, a required label and a 48 dp target so Home, Activity and Receipt are fixed at once, with labels from docs/design/copy.md; the custom Toggle gets switch role and state; inputs get labels; Payment sent is announced on both platforms; the masked balance, the logo label and the activity rows are named properly. The app-wide allowFontScaling=false is reported as a top-severity failure that conflicts with the accepted ADR 0004 and the fixed-height balance card that motivated it. The one-tap Send with no review step (3.3.4) and the portrait lock (1.3.4) are reported. Spoken text not in copy.md is flagged for design, and the edited code holds together on reading since it cannot be type-checked. The write-up separates fixed from open, lists the checks that need VoiceOver, TalkBack and the largest text size on a device, and claims no conformance or check result it did not obtain. Nothing can be built or run here (no node_modules, no device) and nothing is installed; nothing is committed.
expectations: The written audit (saved in the repository or given in full in the final message) covers all five screens: app/(tabs)/index.tsx, app/(tabs)/activity.tsx, app/(tabs)/settings.tsx, app/send.tsx and app/receipt/[id].tsx, and also the tab bar in app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx

Each finding in the audit names the file (and the line or the component) and the WCAG 2.2 success criterion or platform guideline it fails; a finding that is advisory rather than a failure is labelled as advisory (or best practice) and still names its file, but needs no success criterion. A finding named only by screen or area (such as Send, or Home chart) fails this. The audit marks which findings were fixed in this run and which remain open

The audit reports that app/_layout.tsx sets allowFontScaling to false on Text and TextInput for the whole app, so no screen follows the user's system text size (WCAG 1.4.4 Resize text), and places it in the highest or second-highest severity level of the audit's own scale

The run notices that docs/adr/0004-disable-font-scaling.md (Accepted) is why font scaling is off: it either leaves the setting in place and reports it as an open finding that needs that decision revisited, or re-enables scaling and says that this reverses ADR 0004, recording any new decision as Proposed; it does not silently change the setting without mentioning the ADR

The audit or the fix addresses the cause ADR 0004 names: the fixed `height: 120` on the Home balance card in app/(tabs)/index.tsx that clips text at large sizes; if scaling is re-enabled, that fixed height is removed or replaced with a minimum height
The icon-only tab bar (tabBarShowLabel: false in app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx) is reported, and if fixed each tab gets the name Home, Activity or Settings (tabBarAccessibilityLabel, or showing the labels)

src/components/IconButton.tsx is fixed at the component (a button role and an accessibility label passed by every caller, for example a required label prop), and every one of its three call sites supplies a label from docs/design/copy.md: Hide balance or Show balance on Home depending on state, Show incoming payments only for the Activity filter, Share receipt on the receipt screen; a label derived from the handler or icon name (such as filter, onFilt, eye or share-outline) fails this

IconButton's 28 by 28 point hit area is reported as below the 44 pt (iOS) and 48 dp (Android) minimum, and if fixed the effective target reaches at least 48 on Android (for example hitSlop of 10 or more, or a 48 minimum size); a hitSlop of 8, which reaches 44 only, passes only if the audit states it still falls short of 48 dp

The masked balance on Home (the text "••••••" shown when the balance is hidden) is reported as read aloud as bullet characters or with no meaning, and if fixed carries an accessible label such as Balance hidden
The Home wordmark image's accessibilityLabel="logo" is reported as a meaningless name, and if fixed says the product name (Pocketline) or hides the image as decorative

The Activity list rows (a Pressable in app/(tabs)/activity.tsx holding separate Text nodes for payee, time and amount, which opens a receipt) are reported as having no role, so a screen reader does not announce them as something that opens a receipt; and if fixed each row has a button or link role and one label that combines payee, time and amount, with the amount's sign stated in words (paid or received, or minus) rather than left to the "-$23.10" string. The finding need not claim the row is read in separate pieces

The custom Toggle in src/components/Toggle.tsx used for biometric sign-in on Settings is reported as having no role, name or state, and if fixed it exposes a switch role, its checked state and the name of its row (Sign in with Face ID or fingerprint)
The native Switch for Payment notifications in app/(tabs)/settings.tsx is reported as having no accessible name tied to its visible text, and if fixed gets that name
The two TextInputs in app/send.tsx are reported as having only placeholders for a name, and if fixed carry the labels Recipient and Amount in dollars from docs/design/copy.md

The Payment sent confirmation and the validation error in app/send.tsx are reported as not announced to screen readers, and if fixed are announced on iOS as well as Android (accessibilityLiveRegion alone is Android only; AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility or accessibilityRole alert covers iOS)

The audit reports that Send money in app/send.tsx sends a payment on one tap with no review, confirmation or undo step, as a failure of 3.3.4 Error prevention (legal, financial, data), and leaves it open or adds a confirmation step
The audit reports the portrait orientation lock in app.json as a 1.3.4 Orientation finding (open unless portrait is shown to be essential)

The audit states measured contrast for src/theme.ts: muted #9aa0a6 on #ffffff at about 2.6:1 (used for 12 and 13 pt text, fails 4.5:1) and error #ef4444 on #ffffff at about 3.8:1 (14 pt error text, fails 4.5:1)
The audit reports that colors.border #e5e7eb on #ffffff (about 1.2:1) is the only boundary of the Send inputs or the off state of the custom Toggle track, and fails 1.4.11 Non-text contrast (3:1)
The audit does not report as failing any colour pair that passes: success #15803d on white (about 5.0:1), white text on accent #1d4ed8 (about 6.7:1) and text #111827 on white all pass 4.5:1

The SpendChart on Home is reported as conveying data with no text alternative; if fixed, its accessible description is built from the chart's own data (the months and totals), not a generic label such as chart or spending graph

The audit lists the checks that cannot be done from source and need a device (VoiceOver and TalkBack reading order and announcements, the largest system text size), says they were not performed, and does not state that the app conforms to WCAG 2.2 AA or EN 301 549. Every verification result the audit or the final message reports (such as a type check, a lint or a test passing) was obtained in this run without a step the task rules out; a result that rests on an install or network fetch (for example "tsc --noEmit passes" after pnpm installed dependencies) fails this

Spoken text the run adds that docs/design/copy.md does not provide (for example the Activity row label pattern, a name for the masked balance, the chart description, the switch names on Settings) is flagged for design: added to docs/design/copy.md marked as proposed, or listed in the audit or final message as wording for design to confirm. Names taken from visible text on the screen need no flag; user-facing strings invented silently fail this

Because nothing can be type-checked here, the edited code holds together on reading the diff: every prop a change makes required (on IconButton, SpendChart or Toggle) is supplied at every call site, every new API used (such as AccessibilityInfo) is imported from its package, no JSX is left unbalanced, and no accessibility prop or value is used that React Native 0.76 (the version in package.json) does not support

The run installs nothing and fetches nothing from the network (judged from the transcript: no pnpm, npm or yarn install, and no package script run while node_modules is absent, since pnpm installs before running one), no node_modules or lockfile is left in the repository, and the final message says that type checking and tests were not run; it does not claim the edited code builds
package.json is unchanged (no new dependency); app.json is unchanged unless the orientation lock is removed as a reported fix
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
